status_summary: HHS published restated Office of General Counsel organization statements on 2025-03-14 and 2026-09-29, each rescinding all prior statements of organization; both describe an OGC division that advises on civil rights and conscience laws and serves as counsel to OCR, without stating that OGC enforces conscience laws. HHS reorganized OCR effective 2026-06-28 with a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division. No rescission of the PREP Act memo, the eviction moratorium analysis or the Bowen analysis was found, and no source read describes a specific delegation of conscience or RFRA enforcement being returned from OGC to OCR.

HHS Office for Civil Rights reorganization took effect, creating a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division (published 2026-06-30).

HHS published a further restated OGC organization statement that rescinds all prior statements; it describes a division advising on civil rights and conscience laws and legal services to OCR (publication date).

title: Rescind HHS OGC memos on PREP Act, eviction moratorium, newborns and OCR conscience role
uncertainties: The 2026-09-29 OGC statement (91 FR 61422, filed 2026-09-28) was re-read in review: it rescinds all prior statements of organization, assigns the Civil Rights and Health Information Privacy Division an advisory role on civil rights, conscience and religious freedom laws and legal services to OCR, does not name RFRA, mentions the Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness Act only as an area of advice to ASPR, does not mention eviction, Bowen or newborns, and states no effective date. The 2025-03-14 OGC statement and the OCR statement were read in earlier review; neither describes what changed, so whether an earlier statement moved conscience enforcement to OGC and is now superseded cannot be confirmed from these texts. Federal Register API searches since 2025-01-20 on delegation and conscience for HHS returned nine documents with no separate delegation notice, and a review variant on the PREP Act, General Counsel and rescission returned none. Internal OGC memos on the PREP Act, the eviction moratorium and Bowen are not public, so their rescission cannot be checked from public sources and the record rests on absence of evidence; the Unified Agenda, Congress and news checks of a full systematic review were not run. Timeline dates for the OGC notices are Federal Register publication dates.
